commits.title: Script bytes run by idle are held on four store pages and four admin screens

changes.how: A helper for specs, Chromium only. Export async function runBytes(page, path, options?: { cpu?: number }): it opens a CDP session (page.context().newCDPSession(page)); when options.cpu is given it sends Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate with { rate: options.cpu }; starts page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false }); adds an init script that collects 'longtask' entries with a PerformanceObserver into window.__long and the largest-contentful-paint entry's startTime into window.__lcp; goes to the path with waitUntil 'load'; waits for network idle (catch a timeout) and then 3,000 ms, exactly as docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs does; stops coverage. It returns { runBytes: for every coverage entry whose url is a script of this origin, the sum over its functions of the bytes of ranges with count above 0, counting each byte of the file once (merge overlapping ranges: build a boolean array per file or sort and merge), blockingMs: the sum over long tasks of (duration minus 50), lcpMs: window.__lcp rounded }. Copy the range-merging from measure-routes.mjs if it has one; if it does not, write it here and test it in the spec with a tiny synthetic input.

At the end of the file add a describe block 'script run by idle'. A constant RUN_BYTES: Record<string, number> for the home /s/demo/no, a product /s/demo/no/p/demo-keramikkopp, a listing /s/demo/no/products and the cart /s/demo/no/cart, each holding today's measured figure (run the test once with the figure 0 to read it from the failure message, then write it in). For each: runBytes(page, path) at a phone's size (viewport 390 by 844, isMobile, as measure-routes.mjs's PHONE) and expect the figure to be within 5% of the constant, both ways: above fails with 'more script runs before idle: find what was added'; below by more than 5% fails with 'less script runs: lower RUN_BYTES in this file'. Skip the block when the browser is not Chromium (test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium')). Add one test of the merge function: two overlapping ranges 0-10 and 5-20 give 20 bytes.

Model it on e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts (same imports, test.use({ storageState: OWNER.state }), the same way of finding a product id and a page id of the e2e store). At desktop width (1440 by 900) and with the CPU slowed four times (runBytes(page, path, { cpu: 4 })), load four screens: the store's home /admin/{store}, its orders /admin/{store}/orders, a product's editor /admin/{store}/products/{id} and the page builder /admin/{store}/pages/{id}. Hold runBytes for each within 5% of a constant ADMIN_RUN_BYTES in the file, as above. Record lcpMs and blockingMs with test.info().annotations and print them (console.log one line per screen: 'admin-run <screen> lcp=<ms> blocking=<ms> run=<bytes>'). Assert lcpMs for the home and for orders is at most 2,500 only when the environment variable ADMIN_PAINT_BAR is '1' (the bar is judged after phase 2; until then the figure is printed, not enforced: say so in the test's comment).

Add a second run. Read a flag from the third argument's JSON: { slow: true }. When set, for the pages named store-home, store-product, store-products, store-cart-empty (phone) and admin-home, admin-orders, admin-product-editor, admin-page-builder (desktop, signed in), send Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate { rate: 4 } on the page's CDP session before page.goto, collect long tasks with an init script as e2e/run-bytes.ts does, and add to each page's record: blockingMs and runBytes (the script bytes run by idle, from the JS coverage the script already collects). Write them into the same output JSON under a key 'slow'. Without the flag the script behaves exactly as today.

commits.title: A nightly workflow measures four production pages on a phone and keeps the figures

changes.how: Add three options, leaving today's behaviour unchanged when none is given. --runs=N (default 1): run Lighthouse N times per form and report the run whose performance score is the median. --only=performance: with it, --min compares only the performance score (today --min fails on any of the four category scores) and Lighthouse is asked for that category alone ('--only-categories=performance'). --json=<file>: append one JSON line to the file per page and form: { url, form, date (ISO day), score, lcpMs (audits['largest-contentful-paint'].numericValue rounded), blockingMs (audits['total-blocking-time'].numericValue rounded), cls (audits['cumulative-layout-shift'].numericValue to 3 decimals) }. Accept several addresses: every argument that does not start with '--' is a target, measured one after another; the exit code is 1 if any target is under --min. Update the comment block at the top with the three options.

Plain Node. It reads perf-history.json in the working directory if it exists (an array of nights: { date, pages: [{ url, score, lcpMs, blockingMs, cls }] }), reads the JSON-lines file perf.mjs just wrote (path from the first argument), appends tonight, keeps the last 30 nights, and writes perf-history.json back. It prints a Markdown table of the last 7 nights per page. It exits 1 only when, for some page, tonight's score and the previous night's score are both under the line given as --min (default 90): 'two nights in a row under the line', naming the page and both scores. Export the decision as a pure function failingPages(history, min) so it can be tested.

Unit test of failingPages(): one night under 90 gives none; two nights in a row under 90 for the same page gives that page; under, over, under gives none; a page that is missing on one night is not counted as under.

Copy .github/workflows/live-a11y.yml and change: name 'Live performance'; schedule cron '41 3 * * *' (night in Europe, outside the busy hours); the same container image, permissions (contents: read) and install steps. Steps after 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile': (1) uses: actions/cache/restore@v4 with path perf-history.json, key 'perf-history-${{ github.run_id }}' and restore-keys 'perf-history-' (it restores the newest earlier history). (2) run: node scripts/perf.mjs --form=mobile --only=performance --runs=3 --json=perf-tonight.jsonl "$HOME_URL" "$PRODUCT_URL" "$LISTING_URL" https://kaizenaflow.com/ with continue-on-error: true, and env: PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH set to the Chromium of the image (run 'node -e "console.log(require(\'playwright-core\').chromium.executablePath())"' in a step before and write it to $GITHUB_ENV), and the three addresses as workflow-level env values: the home, one product page and the All products listing of the launch-theme demo store that step 1.6 chose, in production (https://<its slug>.kaizenstore.site/<market>...; read the slug and the product's handle from step 1.6's section in docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11.md or its spec). (3) run: node scripts/perf-nightly.mjs perf-tonight.jsonl --min=90 >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY". (4) if: always(), uses: actions/cache/save@v4 with path perf-history.json and key 'perf-history-${{ github.run_id }}'. (5) if: always(), uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with name perf-history and path perf-history.json. Add workflow_dispatch so it can be run by hand. No secret is used: it reads public pages only.

Add a section '## Time on a slow phone': what is held in the build (RUN_BYTES in e2e/performance.spec.ts and ADMIN_RUN_BYTES in e2e/signed-in/admin-run.spec.ts, within 5%), what is printed (blocking time and largest paint with the CPU slowed four times), and the nightly production job (.github/workflows/live-perf.yml: four pages, the median of three runs each, red after two nights in a row under 90).
